United States Infantry Colors as depicted in National Geographic, 1917

The flag's official proportions are 33:26, which is notably shorter than many other state flags. However, in practice, the flag is often produced and sold in 5:3 ratios.[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Greater_coat_of_arms_of_the_United_States.svg/250px-Greater_coat_of_arms_of_the_United_States.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Greater_coat_of_arms_of_the_United_States.svg)

The greater coat of arms of the United States of America.

According to state law, the design of the flag mirrors that of the First North Dakota Infantry's standard during the [Spanish–American War](/wiki/Spanish%E2%80%93American_War "Spanish–American War") and the [Philippine–American War](/wiki/Philippine%E2%80%93American_War "Philippine–American War").[[5]](#cite_note-hist-5) This makes the flag similar to [the greater coat of arms of the United States](/wiki/Great_Seal_of_the_United_States "Great Seal of the United States"), and nearly identical to many other regimental standards, [and current state flags](/wiki/Seal_on_a_bedsheet "Seal on a bedsheet").

A banner with the national coat of arms was carried by all infantry regiments from 1890 to 1904, with the sole distinction being the unit designation inscribed on the scroll underneath the coat of arms.[[6]](#cite_note-ReferenceA-6) The regimental colors of the North Dakotan troops, for instance, were adorned with the inscription "1st North Dakota Infantry".

It is one of nine U.S. state flags to feature an eagle, alongside those of [Illinois](/wiki/Flag_of_Illinois "Flag of Illinois"), [Iowa](/wiki/Flag_of_Iowa "Flag of Iowa"), [Michigan](/wiki/Flag_of_Michigan "Flag of Michigan"), [Missouri](/wiki/Flag_of_Missouri "Flag of Missouri"), [New York](/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_New_York "Coat of arms of New York"), [Oregon]

**Paul Anthony Pierce** (born October 13, 1977) is an American former professional [basketball](/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player. He played 19 seasons in the [National Basketball Association](/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA), predominantly with the [Boston Celtics](/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics").

Pierce was a high school [McDonald's All-American](/wiki/McDonald%27s_All-American "McDonald's All-American") before earning consensus first-team [All-America](/wiki/NCAA_Men%27s_Basketball_All-Americans "NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans") honors as a [junior](/wiki/Junior_(education_year) "Junior (education year)") playing [college basketball](/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for the [Kansas Jayhawks](/wiki/Kansas_Jayhawks_men%27s_basketball "Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball"). After being chosen by the Boston Celtics with the 10th overall pick in the [1998 NBA draft](/wiki/1998_NBA_draft "1998 NBA draft"), Pierce spent the first 15 years of his career with Boston. Pierce's nickname, "**the Truth**," was given to him by [Shaquille O'Neal](/wiki/Shaquille_O%27Neal "Shaquille O'Neal") in 2001. He earned 10 [All-Star](/wiki/NBA_All-Star_Game "NBA All-Star Game") selections and became a four-time [All-NBA](/wiki/All-NBA "All-NBA") team member throughout his 19 year career. Pierce combined with [Kevin Garnett](/wiki/Kevin_Garnett "Kevin Garnett") and [Ray Allen](/wiki/Ray_Allen "Ray Allen") in 2007 to form a "Big Three" that led Boston to two [NBA Finals](/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") and an [NBA championship in 2008](/wiki/2008_NBA_Finals "2008 NBA Finals"). Pierce was named [NBA Finals Most Valuable Player](/wiki/Bill_Russell_NBA_Finals_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Bill Russell NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award") in 2008. In 2021, Pierce was honored by being named to the [NBA 75th Anniversary Team](/wiki/NBA_75th_Anniversary_Team "NBA 75th Anniversary Team") and was inducted into the [Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame](/wiki/Naismith_Memorial_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame").

As of 2024, Barcelona has a population of 1,686,208,[[87]](#cite_note-population2-88) on a land area of 101.4 km2 (39 sq mi). It is the main component of an [administrative area of Greater Barcelona](/wiki/%C3%80rea_Metropolitana_de_Barcelona "Àrea Metropolitana de Barcelona"), with a population of 3,218,071 in an area of 636 km2 (246 sq mi) (density 5,060 inhabitants/km2). The population of the urban area was 4,840,000.[[4]](#cite_note-demographia-4) It is the central nucleus of the [Barcelona metropolitan area](/wiki/Barcelona_metropolitan_area "Barcelona metropolitan area"), which relies on a population of 5,474,482.[[5]](#cite_note-eurostat-5)

In 1900, Barcelona had a population of 533,000,[[73]](#cite_note-gec_3-74) which grew steadily but slowly until 1950, when it started absorbing a high number of people from other less-industrialized parts of Spain. Barcelona's population peaked in 1979 at 1,906,998, and fell throughout the 1980s and 1990s as more people sought a higher [quality of life](/wiki/Quality_of_life "Quality of life") in outlying cities in the Barcelona Metropolitan Area. Bastille debuted in July 2010 with their limited edition 7" single that featured the two tracks "Flaws" and "Icarus". Released through London-based independent record label Young & Lost Club, only 300 copies were pressed.[[7]](#cite_note-7) One of the copies found its way into the hands of Alex Baker, presenter of the unsigned/independent artists radio show on Kerrang! Radio. Baker started to support Bastille on air, and the band began to find an audience. They released the EP *[Laura Palmer](/wiki/Laura_Palmer_EP "Laura Palmer EP")* themselves later in 2011.[[8]](#cite_note-8) After releasing further tracks online through sites such as YouTube and MySpace, the band's audience started to grow.[[9]](#cite_note-:1-9) In December 2011, Smith signed a contract with Virgin Records.[[3]](#cite_note-:0-3) The group subsequently secured a few support slots and later performed at major UK festivals including [Glastonbury](/wiki/Glastonbury_Festival "Glastonbury Festival"), the [Isle of Wight](/wiki/Isle_of_Wight_Festival "Isle of Wight Festival"), [Redfest](/wiki/Redfest "Redfest"), [Reading and Leeds Festival](/wiki/Reading_and_Leeds_Festivals "Reading and Leeds Festivals") and [Blissfields](/wiki/Blissfields "Blissfields"). The band also recorded and released two parts of their mix-tape titled *Other People's Heartache* for free.[[9]](#cite_note-:1-9)

Quaker Oats Company :: History :: Quaker Oats Company :: part 02 :: chunk_0003
In 1982, Quaker Oats purchased [US Games](/wiki/US_Games "US Games"), a company that created games for the [Atari 2600](/wiki/Atari_2600 "Atari 2600"). It went out of business after one year. That same year, Quaker Oats acquired Florida-based orange juice plant Ardmore Farms, which it would own until selling it to [Country Pure Foods](/wiki/Country_Pure_Foods "Country Pure Foods") in 1998.[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15)

In 1983, Quaker bought Stokely-Van Camp, Inc., makers of [Van Camp's](/wiki/Van_Camp%27s "Van Camp's") and [Gatorade](/wiki/Gatorade "Gatorade").[[16]](#cite_note-16)

Quaker bought [Snapple](/wiki/Snapple "Snapple") for $1.7 billion in 1994 and sold it to [Triarc](/wiki/Wendy%27s/Arby%27s_Group "Wendy's/Arby's Group") in 1997 for $300 million.[[17]](#cite_note-17) Triarc sold it to [Cadbury Schweppes](/wiki/Cadbury_Schweppes "Cadbury Schweppes") for $1.45 billion in September 2000.[[18]](#cite_note-18) It was spun off in May 2008 to its current owners, [Dr Pepper Snapple Group](/wiki/Dr_Pepper_Snapple_Group "Dr Pepper Snapple Group").

In 1996, Quaker spun off its frozen food business, selling it to Aurora Foods (which was bought by [Pinnacle Foods](/wiki/Pinnacle_Foods "Pinnacle Foods") in 2004).

In August 2001, Quaker Oats was acquired by [PepsiCo](/wiki/PepsiCo "PepsiCo") for $14 billion,[[19]](#cite_note-19) primarily for the Gatorade brand.

Starting in 1987 through the 1990s, actor [Wilford Brimley](/wiki/Wilford_Brimley "Wilford Brimley") appeared in television commercials for Quaker. In the commercials, he extolled the virtues and healthfulness of oat consumption, sometimes to a young child. "It's the right thing to do" was a common slogan during the commercials.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

Plant suffered a broken ankle and Maureen was badly injured; a blood transfusion saved her life.[[77]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavis1985354–355-82) Unable to tour, he headed to the [Channel Island](/wiki/Channel_Island "Channel Island") of [Jersey](/wiki/Jersey "Jersey") to spend August and September recuperating, with Bonham and Page in tow. The band then reconvened in [Malibu, California](/wiki/Malibu,_California "Malibu, California"). During this forced hiatus, much of the material for their next album, *[Presence](/wiki/Presence_(album) "Presence (album)")*, was written.[[78]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWall2008364-83)

By this time, Led Zeppelin were the world's number one rock attraction,[[79]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELewis200345-84) having outsold most bands of the time, including the Rolling Stones.[[80]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavis1985173-85) *Presence*, released in March 1976, marked a change in the Led Zeppelin sound towards more straightforward, guitar-based jams, departing from the acoustic ballads and intricate arrangements featured on their previous albums. Main article: [Sam's Club](/wiki/Sam%27s_Club "Sam's Club")

**Sam's Club** is a chain of [warehouse clubs](/wiki/Warehouse_club "Warehouse club") that sell groceries and [general merchandise](/wiki/General_merchandise "General merchandise"), often in bulk.[[32]](#cite_note-Volpe-36) Locations generally range in size from 32,000–168,000 sq ft (3,000–15,600 m2), with an average club size of approximately 134,000 sq ft (12,400 m2).[[151]](#cite_note-2022_10-K-155) The first Sam's Club was opened by Walmart, Inc. in 1983 in [Midwest City, Oklahoma](/wiki/Midwest_City,_Oklahoma "Midwest City, Oklahoma")[[291]](#cite_note-aboutsamsclub-295) under the name "Sam's Wholesale Club". The chain was named after its founder Sam Walton. As of October 31, 2022, Sam's Club operated 600 membership warehouse clubs and accounted for 11.3% of Walmart's revenue at $57.839 billion in fiscal year 2019.[[292]](#cite_note-xbrlus_1-296)[[293]](#cite_note-297) Christopher Nicholas is the president and CEO of Sam's Club.[[150]](#cite_note-leadership-154)[[294]](#cite_note-298)

Based in San Bruno, California, Walmart's Global eCommerce division provides online retailing for Walmart, Sam's Club, and all other international brands. There are several U.S. locations in California and Oregon: [San Bruno](/wiki/San_Bruno,_California "San Bruno, California"), [Sunnyvale](/wiki/Sunnyvale,_California "Sunnyvale, California"), [Brisbane](/wiki/Brisbane,_California "Brisbane, California"), and [Portland](/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon"). Locations outside of the United States include [Shanghai](/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai") (China), [Leeds](/wiki/Leeds "Leeds") (United Kingdom), and [Bangalore](/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore") (India).
